chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from some of his companions, from Mudrik al-Hazhaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
a man who has sheep and gives them in exchange for a known quantity of wool, butter/ghee, or dirhams. He said, 'There is no objection to the dirhams,' but he disliked the butter/ghee.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to trade sheep for butter or dirhams in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding *Qard al-Hasan* or livestock leasing, distinguishing between permissible and disliked forms of return. While receiving fixed dirhams is deemed sound, receiving butter (*saman*) is disliked, likely due to the potential for *Gharar* (uncertainty) in the quality or quantity of the perishable commodity compared to the stability of currency. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on minimizing ambiguity in agricultural and trade contracts to ensure fairness between the owner and the caretaker.
